H2.title: Summary state cue drifts from the ingest fragment it claims to share
H2.resolution: ROUND 2 - the behaviour is closed, not just the claim. Round 1 corrected the false 'the cue cannot drift from the fragment by construction' comment and deliberately kept the page-load snapshot; a cue that lies is a defect whether or not the comment admits it, and the owner's decision on re-review was to fix it properly. _ingest_status_fragment now appends a TOP-LEVEL <code id="ingest-state-cue" hx-swap-oob="true"> carrying that branch's OWN literal status token, so every response that re-renders the body also re-renders the cue: the 2s poll (H2's direction - `running` over a settled success body), the terminal 286 that stops the poll, and the 202 returned when a run is started in-page (M2's sharper direction - `success`/`none` over a live run). The cue is NOT a second read of the row: it is the fragment's own token, so there is one reader and nothing left to disagree with. Guarded by TestSummaryCueIsRefreshedOutOfBand in tests/test_ui_m12_corpus_before_machinery.py - every branch parametrised, plus a top-level-position guard, because a NESTED hx-swap-oob is inert and would fail exactly like the original bug.

history.resolution: the false 'the cue cannot drift from the fragment by construction' claim corrected in BOTH places it appeared - the template comment and the guard docstring. What cannot drift is the SOURCE row; the rendered value is a page-load snapshot with no hx-swap-oob anywhere in server/. The snapshot is kept deliberately per the owner's decision; the defect was the claim, not the tradeoff
